habitat: Scrub forest; deciduous/moist deciduous forests; densely wooded lowlands and foothills
story: Few birds capture the imagination quite like the Jungle Owlet (Glaucidium radiatum). As a member of the Strigidae family, it has carved out a unique niche in Scrub forest; deciduous/moist deciduous forests; densely wooded lowlands and foothills. Its conservation status is Least Concern (LC), a classification that drives crucial research and protection efforts. The Jungle Owlet's presence is a vital sign of its ecosystem's health, making its preservation a priority. This poster is a tribute to the Jungle Owlet, celebrating its role in the natural world and inspiring a deeper appreciation for biodiversity.
